title: Contributing to phiper
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("Polymerase3/phiper", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). title: Alpha Diversity Analysis in PhIP-seq
text: Alpha diversity quantifies within-sample variety reactive peptides. PhIP-seq, sample’s enrichment profile can characterised many unique peptide species enriched (richness), evenly enrichment distributed (evenness), dominated single peptide (dominance). properties change across disease conditions, timepoints, patient subgroups, making alpha diversity useful summary statistic exploratory analysis hypothesis testing. vignette walks complete alpha diversity workflow phiper: Computing diversity metrics compute_alpha() Visualising distributions plot_alpha() plot_alpha_interactive() Testing group differences compute_alpha_significance() Summarising statistical results plot_alpha_significance()

text: Threshold mode re-defines “present” using continuous abundance column (fold_change default). peptides whose fold-change exceeds threshold counted. Raising threshold sharpens definition “hit” typically reduces richness. Supply abundance_col use different column fold_change:
code: # Loose threshold: fold_change > 10 alpha_thr10 <- compute_alpha(   pd,   group_cols = "group",   ranks      = "peptide_id",   mode       = "threshold",   threshold  = 10,   metrics    = "richness" ) #> [10:27:35] INFO  Computing alpha diversity (<phip_data>) #>                  -> group_cols: 'group'; ranks: 'peptide_id' #> [10:27:36] OK    Computing alpha diversity (<phip_data>) - done #>                  -> elapsed: 0.238s  # Strict threshold: fold_change > 100 alpha_thr100 <- compute_alpha(   pd,   group_cols = "group",   ranks      = "peptide_id",   mode       = "threshold",   threshold  = 100,   metrics    = "richness" ) #> [10:27:36] INFO  Computing alpha diversity (<phip_data>) #>                  -> group_cols: 'group'; ranks: 'peptide_id' #> [10:27:36] OK    Computing alpha diversity (<phip_data>) - done #>                  -> elapsed: 0.234s  # Richness drops as the threshold increases data.frame(   mode      = c("binary", "threshold > 10", "threshold > 100"),   mean_richness = c(     mean(alpha_bin$group$richness),     mean(alpha_thr10$group$richness),     mean(alpha_thr100$group$richness)   ) ) #>              mode mean_richness #> 1          binary      233.8375 #> 2  threshold > 10      949.6750 #> 3 threshold > 100      676.3750 alpha_thr_counts <- compute_alpha(   pd,   group_cols    = "group",   ranks         = "peptide_id",   mode          = "threshold",   abundance_col = "counts_hits",   threshold     = 50 )

Test sig <- compute_alpha_significance(alpha, group_col = "group")  # 4. what: Prevalence by group with pairwise tests (POP; per-rank FDR; BH & weighted BH) — ph_prevalence_compare
title: Prevalence by group with pairwise tests (POP; per-rank FDR; BH & weighted BH) — ph_prevalence_compare
text: Computes prevalence (counts, proportions, percentages) features defined requested rank_cols across one grouping "universes" (group_cols, optional interaction), performs pairwise statistical tests group levels. Presence computed k--n POP rule within sample (pop_k_min, default 1). Two testing modes supported: Unpaired: Fisher’s exact test (2×2) per (rank, feature, group pair). Paired: McNemar’s exact (binomial) per subject (paired = TRUE requires subject_id). P-values adjusted per rank (single FDR family rank across requested universes/pairs/features) using BH optional weighted BH (weight_mode = "peptide_count").

NOTE: can also character scalar naming column links related samples (e.g. "subject_id" "dyade"). , samples present groups identifier used paired McNemar tests. peptide_library Optional peptide metadata table used map non-peptide rank columns. NULL, function use x$peptide_library.

text: object class ph_prev_result, .e., tibble (lazy table collect = FALSE unpaired path) attributes: prev_meta$m_by_rank: named integer vector m_r per rank, prev_meta$pairs_by_universe: tibble group_col, k_levels, n_pairs, prev_meta$pool_by_rank: tibble rank, POOL, bookkeeping: paired, weight_mode, pop_k_min, fdr_scope = "per-rank", register_name (unpaired path) view (available). Columns include (subset may differ paths): view, rank, feature, n_peptides, group_col, group1, group2, n1, N1, prop1, percent1, n2, N2, prop2, percent2, optional ratio, delta_ratio, p_raw, p_adj_rank, passed_rank_bh, category_rank_bh, p_adj_rank_wbh, passed_rank_wbh, category_rank_wbh.

title: Prevalence by group with pairwise tests (POP; per-rank FDR; BH & weighted BH) — ph_prevalence_compare
text: universe construction. group_col create universe levels present data (non-missing). interaction = TRUE (combine_cols provided), also build combined universe group value <col1>::<col2>. Denominators N distinct sample counts per (group_col, group_value). presence (pop). sample (rank, feature), count number positive peptides contributing feature; feature marked present k >= pop_k_min (default 1). yields n_present per (group_col, group_value, rank, feature) prevalence prop = n_present / N. pairwise tests. universe K levels form unordered pairs K*(K-1)/2. (rank, feature, pair): unpaired: build 2×2 table (n1, N1 - n1, n2, N2 - n2) run Fisher’s exact test (two-sided). paired: compute discordant counts (n01, n10) per subject run McNemar’s exact binomial test (binom.test(n01, n01+n10)). fdr families number comparisons. Let POOL_r number unique features given rank r across requested universes (presence aggregation missing value filtering). Let PAIRS = sum_u K_u*(K_u-1)/2 total number unordered level-pairs summed universes u (u one group_col interaction universe). size single FDR family rank r : $$ m_r \;=\; POOL_r \times PAIRS. $$ p-values produced rank r (covering universes level pairs) adjusted together one family size m_r. makes per-rank FDR stricter () many features rank, /(ii) many universes levels generate many pairwise comparisons. bh (benjamini–hochberg). Within rank r (view present), BH q-values computed via p.adjust(method="BH") vector p-values length m_r (excluding NAs). Reported columns: p_adj_rank, passed_rank_bh, category_rank_bh. weighted bh. weight_mode="peptide_count", (rank,feature) gets base weight equal number distinct peptides mapping feature. Within rank r (view present), weights scaled sum m_r: $$ w_i^{*} \;=\; w_i \cdot \frac{m_r}{\sum_j w_j}. $$ adjust using standard weighted step-rule \(p_i / w_i^{*}\). resulting q-values reported p_adj_rank_wbh, flags passed_rank_wbh labels category_rank_wbh. weight_mode="none", weights 1 wBH reduces BH. logging comparisons. function logs: POOL_r per rank, number levels K_u pair counts per universe, PAIRS = sum_u K_u*(K_u-1)/2, m_r = POOL_r * PAIRS rank. values also returned object metadata (see Value).
